question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate beyond plugin `before_tool_call.requireApproval`, and what contract should own risk tiers plus assistant-text-aware gating?
rationale: This changes the host authorization boundary, config schema, tool execution ordering, transcript semantics, and channel approval UX, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Design core confirmation policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and define a core confirmation contract that reuses existing approval plumbing while adding deterministic risk tiers and same-response text handling.

options.title: Route to plugin-only policy
options.body: Treat plugin `requireApproval` as the intended extension point and close only after maintainers explicitly decide core will not own a global gate.

options.title: Narrow to concrete bugs
options.body: Leave broad confirmation design unimplemented and handle reports like unintended config edits through narrower tool policy or exec approval fixes.

recommendation.title: Design core confirmation policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define a core confirmation contract that reuses existing approval plumbing while adding deterministic risk tiers and same-response text handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent work and timeline mentions point to this owner for the agent/plugin hook and approval-policy boundary decision.
